newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Ample supplies seen depressing prices.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Ample supplies seen depressing prices.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to slide further this week due to more shipments from Manila and Indonesia, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
Traders also said a weaker peso would compel more coconut oil sellers in the Philippines.
"I expect shipments of at least 95,000 tonnes of coconut oil from the Philippines to Rotterdam this month and an additional 55,000 tonnes from Indonesia," said a senior Manila trader.
MV Stolt Heron, carrying some 23,000 tonnes of coconut oil, left the Philippines last week. Another ship, MV Star Sapphire, is also arriving in the country this week to load another 23,000 tonnes.
Traders said coconut oil buyers remained calm despite the drop in stocks to 285 tonnes on July 14 from the week-ago 3,340.

"A ship carrying 35,000 tonnes of Philippine coconut oil arrived in Rotterdam on June 15 and we expect the arrival of three more ships carrying an additional 65,000 tonnes," said another Manila trader.

Traders said copra farmers were selling more to local crushers following the effective devaluation of the peso by 11.5 percent to 29.45 on July 11. The local currency had since stabilised at 28 pesos.
After the Philippine Central Bank's announcement that it would allow the peso to trade in a wider band, coconut oil prices fell by $25 but recovered by $10 at the end of the week, traders said.
On Monday, Philippine sellers pegged coconut oil at $601.25 per tonne CIF for July/August shipment, trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines said.
Copra prices in Manila fell to 8.80 pesos per kg on Monday from last week's 9.20 pesos as the Philippine peso ended steady at 28 to the dollar.

"Copra farmers jacked up their prices to 9.20 pesos per kg last week from the previous 8.50 as they anticipated windfall crusher profits following the (de facto) devaluation of the peso," said one trader. --Dolly Aglay (63 2) 841-8936, Fax 817-6267
